overall: Atlanta is off to a mild start this Wednesday morning, with temperatures in the mid-to-upper 60s and a running max of just 69.8°F as of 05:04 ET. Skies are mostly clear (only 12% cloud fraction), winds are light, and no precipitation is expected, setting up favorable daytime heating conditions. The Flood Warning alerts are confined to the Satilla River in far southeast Georgia and have no bearing on Atlanta's temperature forecast.
forecast_obs_notes: There is modest spread among the NWP models: HRRR projects 87.5°F (closely matching the NWS official forecast of ~87°F), while ECMWF and NBM are a few degrees cooler at 84.8°F. The META fused model resolves much of this disagreement, placing roughly 69% of probability mass in the 86–91°F range, with the 86–87°F and 88–89°F buckets each carrying ~34.4%—a tight, credible distribution consistent with the NWS narrative.
max_temp_prediction: With mostly sunny skies, light winds, and strong NWS/HRRR alignment near 87°F, today's high is most likely to land in the 86–89°F range. The META model's dual peak at 86–87°F and 88–89°F (combined ~69%) reflects mild uncertainty about exactly how much afternoon heating occurs, but a significant excursion above 90°F or below 85°F appears unlikely given current clear-sky conditions and model consensus. Best estimate is approximately 87°F, with moderate-to-good confidence.
